postGameActualStartingLineup.source: Stats API boxscore (research cache wrapper meta+body)
postGameActualStartingLineup.extractionRule: players[].battingOrder matching /^[1-9]00$/ are original starting batting-order slots 1–9; gameStatus.isSubstitute===false on all 270 starters observed

fieldsObserved.isDH: position.abbreviation==='DH' — available (30/30 sides had DH; universal DH era)
fieldsObserved.battingSide: NOT in boxscore person; available via /api/v1/people/{id}.batSide.code with extra research calls
fieldsObserved.teamIdName: team.team.id / team.team.name — available on team object

playersDotBattingOrder.meaning: Encoded batting-order history. Suffix 00 = original starter for that slot; 01+ (e.g. 801, 301) = later occupants of that slot after PH/PR/defensive replacement.
playersDotBattingOrder.evidence: Across 15 games, *00 always yields exactly 9 non-substitute batters per side; substitutes carry *0[1-9] codes and isSubstitute=true.

teamDotBattingOrder.meaning: Array of 9 personIds reflecting current/final batting order after substitutions — NOT reliable as starting lineup.
teamDotBattingOrder.evidence: 29/30 team-sides mismatched team.battingOrder vs *00 starters (only 1 side unchanged). Example gamePk 823433 home slot 8: final id ≠ starter Gabriel Rincones Jr.

battingOrderSemantics.recommendation: Use players[].battingOrder *00 (+ isSubstitute===false) for postGameActualLineup. Do not use team.battingOrder as starting lineup.
